title: Noetherian approximation of a relative global complete intersection
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n,c\ge0$ integers and $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] such that $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. Then there is a subring $R_0\subseteq R$ which is a finite type $\mathbf Z$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] (that is, generated as a ring by finitely many elements) and contains all coefficients of $f_1,\dots,f_c$, such that, regarding $f_1,\dots,f_c$ as elements of $R_0[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, the ring $R_0[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection over $R_0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SU (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-Noetherian, algebra.tex line 36727) and its proof. Tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags (00SU,algebra-lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-Noetherian)

proof.text: Let $R_0\subseteq R$ be the subring generated by the finitely many coefficients of $f_1,\dots,f_c$ over $\mathbf Z$; it is a finite type $\mathbf Z$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Regard the $f_i$ as polynomials over $R_0$ and put $S_0=R_0[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$. The polynomial scalar-extension isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension] and tensoring a quotient [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] identify $R\otimes_{R_0}S_0$ with $S=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$, carrying each $g\in S_0$ to its image in $S$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SU (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-Noetherian), lines 36739-36743

proof.text: For a prime $\mathfrak q\subset S$, let $\mathfrak p\subset R$, $\mathfrak q_0\subset S_0$ and $\mathfrak p_0\subset R_0$ be its contractions. Put $F_0=S_0\otimes_{R_0}\kappa(\mathfrak p_0)$ and $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Step 1 and tensor reassociation [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] identify $F$ with $F_0\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p_0)}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$; both fibres are nonzero since $\mathfrak q_0$ and $\mathfrak q$ lie over the corresponding base primes [lem-weil-pbc-prime-in-image-iff-fibre-ring-nonzero]. By [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection], $\dim\operatorname{Spec}F=n-c$. This equals $\dim\operatorname{Spec}F_0$: the scalar-extension map $F_0\to F$ is faithfully flat [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat], hence surjective on spectra [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum]; at each point of $\operatorname{Spec}F$, the local dimension equals that at its image in $\operatorname{Spec}F_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-field-extension], and taking suprema over points gives equality of global dimensions [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions]. In particular, the dimension of $\operatorname{Spec}F_0$ at the point determined by $\mathfrak q_0$ is at most $n-c$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SU, lines 36743-36749; dimension comparison is expanded from the cited field-extension result

proof.text: Write $d(\mathfrak q_0)$ for the local dimension of the fibre of $R_0\to S_0$ at $\mathfrak q_0$; Step 2 gives $d(\mathfrak q_0)\le n-c$. The map $R_0\to S_0$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-dimension-neighborhood] at $\mathfrak q_0$ with this actual integer $d(\mathfrak q_0)$: there is $g_{\mathfrak q}\in S_0\setminus\mathfrak q_0$ such that every nonzero fibre of $(S_0)_{g_{\mathfrak q}}$ over $R_0$ has dimension at most $d(\mathfrak q_0)\le n-c$. Its image in $S$ is outside $\mathfrak q$, so $\mathfrak q\in D(g_{\mathfrak q})$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SU, lines 36750-36753; the principal-open bound is the form of Lemma Tag 00QH used in Lemma Tag 00ST, part (3)

proof.text: The opens $D(g_{\mathfrak q})$ from Step 3 pull back to an open cover of $\operatorname{Spec}S$. Its quasi-compactness [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact] gives finitely many $g_1,\dots,g_m\in S_0$ with the same fibre bound on each $(S_0)_{g_j}$ and with $\operatorname{Spec}S=\bigcup_jD(\bar g_j)$, where $\bar g_j$ is the image of $g_j$ in $S$. Choose polynomial lifts $G_j\in R_0[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ of the $g_j$. By the unit-ideal criterion in the same cited node, $1=\sum_j\bar h_j\bar g_j$ for some $\bar h_j\in S$. Lift each $\bar h_j$ to a polynomial $h_j\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$; then $1-\sum_jh_jG_j=\sum_i a_if_i$ for polynomials $a_i\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$. For $S=0$, use the empty cover and the corresponding equation $1=\sum_i a_if_i$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SU, lines 36753-36760; finite-subcover and unit-ideal steps made explicit

proof.text: Enlarge $R_0$ inside $R$ to the subring $R_1$ generated by the coefficients of the $f_i$, $G_j$, $h_j$ and $a_i$ appearing in Step 4. It is still a finite type $\mathbf Z$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Put $S_1=R_1[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ and use $g_j$ also for the image of $G_j$ in $S_1$. The same polynomial equation holds over $R_1$, so these $g_1,\dots,g_m$ generate $1$ in $S_1$ (in the empty-cover case, $S_1=0$). To check that each $(S_1)_{g_j}$ keeps its fibre bound, fix a prime $\mathfrak p_1\subset R_1$ with contraction $\mathfrak p_0\subset R_0$. By Step 1, its fibre is the scalar extension of the corresponding fibre of $(S_0)_{g_j}$ along $\kappa(\mathfrak p_0)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p_1)$. Every point of the new fibre maps to a point of the old fibre, and its local dimension is unchanged by [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-field-extension]. The old local dimensions are at most $n-c$ by Step 3 and [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions], hence the new fibre has dimension at most $n-c$ by the same supremum formula. Since the $D(g_j)$ cover $\operatorname{Spec}S_1$, every nonempty fibre of $R_1\to S_1$ has dimension at most $n-c$: each of its points lies in one of these principal opens, and local dimension is unchanged on an open neighbourhood [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SU, lines 36760-36763; preservation of the local bounds under enlargement and passage from the principal opens to each whole fibre made explicit

proof.text: If $S_1=0$, there are no nonempty fibres and the required relative global complete-intersection condition is vacuous [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. Otherwise $S_1$ has a prime, hence a nonempty fibre; the upper bound in Step 5 forces $c\le n$. For each nonempty fibre over $\mathfrak p_1\subset R_1$, scalar extension of the polynomial presentation gives $\kappa(\mathfrak p_1)[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_c)$ [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension] [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change]. Its dimension is at least $n-c$ by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-quotient-dimension-lower-bound], and at most $n-c$ by Step 5. Thus every nonempty fibre has dimension exactly $n-c$, making $S_1$ a relative global complete intersection [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. Take $R_1$ as the requested subring.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SU, lines 36761-36763; lower bound from the polynomial presentation is made explicit

lean.statement: theorem exists_finiteType_subring_relativeGlobalCompleteIntersection (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (n c : ℕ) (f : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) (h : IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersectionPresentation f) : ∃ (R₀ : Subring R), Algebra.FiniteType ℤ R₀ ∧ ∃ (f₀ : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin n) R₀), (∀ (i : Fin c) (d : Fin n →₀ ℕ), (MvPolynomial.coeff d (f i)) = (((MvPolynomial.coeff d (f₀ i)) : R₀) : R)) ∧ IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersectionPresentation f₀
